title: Theory of optical alignment and orientation of excitons in an ensemble of semiconductor nanoplatelets
authors: O. O. Druzhinina, A. V. Rodina
abstract: We present the theory of exciton optical alignment and optical orientation effects in a single semiconductor nanoplatelet (NPL) and in an ensemble of NPLs. The theoretical model is developed to take into account the emission from both bright and dark exciton states in the case of strong electron-hole exchange interaction and an isotropic distribution of in-plane orientations of the NPLs' edges with respect to the linear polarization axis. The conditions for the linear optical response regime on the polarized resonant excitation of the bright exciton are considered, and the steady-state and time-dependent expressions for polarized photoluminescence are presented for the low temperature case in the Faraday magnetic field at normal incidence. The symmetry of the obtained optical response corresponds to the $C_{2}$ point group for the single NPL and the $C_{\infty}$ point group for the NPL ensemble. The bright-to-dark exciton coupling mechanism allowing one to observe the optical alignment of the dark exciton is considered. The example calculations of the effects are presented for the parameters close to those of CdSe/CdS core/shell NPLs. The effect of the fluctuations in the exciton parameters in the ensemble on the polarization dephasing in the transverse effective magnetic field is demonstrated.
summary: This paper presents a comprehensive theory for understanding how excitons align and orient themselves in semiconductor nanoplatelets. By modeling the coupling between bright and dark exciton states using a pseudospin formalism, the authors predict polarization signatures observable in photoluminescence. This work is crucial for controlling and characterizing spin-related quantum phenomena in solid-state nanostructures.
main_problem: The paper develops a theoretical framework to describe the optical alignment and orientation effects of excitons within single and ensemble semiconductor nanoplatelets (NPLs). It specifically models the interplay between bright and dark exciton states.
main_result: The theory predicts distinct symmetries for the optical response ($C_2$ for a single NPL and $C_{\infty}$ for the ensemble) and shows how bright-to-dark exciton coupling allows for the observation of dark exciton optical alignment.
method: The authors use a density matrix formalism applied to two interacting pseudospins (bright and dark excitons) to calculate time-dependent and steady-state polarized photoluminescence.
model_or_system: The system is semiconductor nanoplatelets (e.g., CdSe/CdS core/shell) whose excitons are modeled using a pseudospin formalism. The Hamiltonian accounts for exchange interactions and Zeeman splitting, while the polarization is analyzed using Stokes parameters.
key_observables: Polarized photoluminescence (PL), Stokes parameters ($P_l, P_{l'}, P_c$), and the degree of exciton optical alignment/orientation.
important_parameters: Low temperature regime, Faraday magnetic field, and the strength of the electron-hole exchange interaction.
main_assumptions: Assumes an isotropic distribution of in-plane NPL edge orientations in the ensemble and treats the system in the linear optical response regime.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the geometry of NPLs (single and ensemble), the axes used for polarization analysis, and the energy splitting/pseudospin evolution in a magnetic field.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the physical system and the need for the theory, developing the pseudospin formalism for bright/dark excitons, deriving the polarization response equations, and finally applying these to analyze specific effects like alignment and ensemble averaging.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems because it models spin dynamics and polarization transfer in solid-state quantum emitters (excitons) under external fields, which is a core topic in quantum light sources.
